title: feat(smtp): wire mail-auth application-level DNS cache
description:
## Why

mail-auth 0.8 has a `ResolverCache` trait for caching parsed SPF/DKIM/DMARC TXT records at the application level. Stoa currently uses `Parameters::new()` which defaults to `NoCache` — every verification re-parses raw DNS TXT bytes into structured SPF policies and DKIM public keys even when hickory-resolver already has the raw response cached. This wastes CPU on repeated parses of the same records.

The fix is purely additive: wire a `DashMap`-backed (or `std::sync::Mutex<HashMap>`-backed) cache into the `SpfParameters` and `DkimParameters` / `DmarcParameters` calls in `crates/smtp/src/auth.rs`. mail-auth already defines the interface; stoa just needs to construct a cache and pass it via the builder methods (`.with_txt_cache()`, `.with_ipv4_cache()`, etc.).

## What

- Add a `DnsCache` struct in `crates/smtp/src/auth.rs` (or a new `crates/smtp/src/dns_cache.rs`) implementing `ResolverCache<Box<str>, Txt>` and the other required types.
- Cache TTL: use the `valid_until: Instant` argument mail-auth passes to `insert()` — evict on read when expired.
- Wire the cache into `verify_inbound`: pass `.with_txt_cache(&cache)` to `SpfParameters`, `DkimParameters`, and `DmarcParameters`.
- Cache instance: created once at startup, stored in `Arc<DnsCache>`, cloned into each session (same pattern as `MessageAuthenticator`).
- No external crate required beyond `dashmap` (already in workspace) or stdlib `Mutex<HashMap>`.

## What stays the same

- Per-connection concurrency model unchanged.
- hickory-resolver DNS-level cache unchanged.
- No config knob needed — the cache is always on when auth is enabled.

## Acceptance criteria

- `verify_inbound` passes a populated cache to all three parameter builders.
- Cache evicts expired entries on read (respects `valid_until`).
- Existing SPF/DKIM/DMARC tests still pass.
- cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings + cargo test --workspace all pass clean.
